chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Abu Ayoub al-Khazzaz, from Abu Ubeyda al-Hazza', who said:

I said to Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), 'Narrate to me with what I can benefit from.' So he (peace be upon him) said: 'O Abu Ubeyda! Frequently remember the death, for a human being would not frequently remember the death except that he would be an ascetic in the world'.

key_terms.زَهِدَ فِي الدُّنْيَا: asceticism in the world / detachment from the world

ai.seo_question: How does remembering death affect one's attitude towards the world according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this hadith from al-Kafi, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) identifies the frequent remembrance of death (dhikr al-mawt) as the primary means to cultivate zuhd (asceticism) and detach from worldly distractions. This teaching underscores the Shia scholarly view that mortality serves as a spiritual catalyst, redirecting focus from transient material gains to eternal spiritual realities. The advice highlights the practical application of introspection in maintaining piety and reducing attachment to dunya.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Isa from Ali Bin Al Hakam, from Abu Ayoub Al Khazzaz, from Abu Ubeyda Al Haza’a who said,

‘I said to Abu Ja’far<sup style="font-weight: normal">asws</sup>, ‘(Please) Narrate to me with what I can benefit from’. So he<sup style="font-weight: normal">asws</sup> said: ‘O Abu Ubeyda! Frequently remember the death, for a human being would not frequent in remembering the death except that he would be an ascetic in the world’.
en.sarwar: 13. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn ‘Isa from Ali ibn al-Hakam from abu Ayyub al-Khazzaz from abu ‘Ubaydah al-Hadhdha’ who has said the following:

“I asked abu Ja’far (a.s.) ‘(I request you to) teach me a Hadith that can benefit me.’ The Imam said, ‘O abu ‘Ubaydah, speak of death very often. No one speaks of death very often but that it reduces his interest in worldly matters.’”
